summary.oneLiner: Eveready Industries India Limited is a 100-year-old Indian consumer brand and the dominant player in dry cell batteries, with over 50% share of the Indian dry cell battery market, a leadership position in branded flashlights and an emerging presence in lighting and electrical products.
summary.business: Eveready makes and sells portable energy and lighting solutions for Indian households and institutions - dry cell batteries (carbon zinc, alkaline, lithium, coin cell and rechargeable), flashlights, and lighting and electrical products. Batteries constitute the majority of the Company's sales, with lighting and flashlights contributing materially to the overall revenue mix. Products reach consumers through an estimated 4.5+ million retail touchpoints nationwide with direct coverage of approximately 0.6 million outlets, supplemented by e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.

currentContext.strengths: Dominant market share of over 50% (approximately 51.4% value share) in the Indian dry cell battery market|Best-in-class pan-India distribution: an estimated 4.5+ million retail touchpoints with direct coverage of approximately 0.6 million outlets|Legacy of over 100 years and strong brand equity/consumer trust in the Eveready name|First-mover advantage in domestic alkaline manufacturing anchored by the Jammu facility, strengthening supply chain control and cost competitiveness|In-house R&D facility at Kolkata under DSIR oversight driving product innovation across segments|Multi-brand portfolio across the value pyramid (Eveready, Ultima, PowerCell, Shakti, Uniross) covering carbon zinc, alkaline, lithium and rechargeable formats|Dominant position in the fast-evolving quick commerce channel, adding to omnichannel presence|Category leadership in mosquito swatters, an adjacency built on brand strength and distribution advantages
currentContext.strategies: Intensify premiumisation across the portfolio through a growing range of alkaline and rechargeable products to strengthen presence in higher-value segments and improve product mix|Scale the greenfield alkaline battery manufacturing capability at Jammu to deliver greater scale, supply reliability and a healthier margin structure, and to reduce import dependence|Use the Jammu facility to expand business through white labelling and serve domestic and international markets, with the stated ambition to emerge as a global player in the alkaline battery segment|Drive innovation and R&D focused on better performance, longer life and improved energy efficiency across batteries, flashlights and lighting solutions|Enhance distribution efficiency: streamline channel structures, strengthen distributor partnerships and make decision-making increasingly data-analytics led for deeper urban and rural penetration and faster replenishment|Build the 'Ultima Pro' and 'Ultima' alkaline ranges as key growth engines, supported by a renewed communication platform and the Company's expansive retail footprint|Actively develop digital commerce channels including e-commerce and quick commerce, particularly in Metro and Tier-1/Tier-2 markets|Expand strategically into adjacent categories such as mobile accessories, power banks and mosquito rackets to deepen household penetration|Allocate capital carefully, prioritising investments that maintain balance sheet stability and sharpen long-term strategic edge, supported by calibrated pricing, tight opex control and prudent working capital management|Sustain operational excellence across manufacturing - stringent quality standards, workplace safety, energy efficiency, structured audits and technology integration|Embed sustainability through energy efficiency in manufacturing, resource optimisation and expansion of high-efficiency and rechargeable products|The Board's stated approach is to reward shareholders through a formal, policy-anchored dividend: a Dividend Distribution Policy is maintained under the SEBI Listing Regulations and published on the Company's website, and the Directors recommended a higher dividend for the financial year ended 31st March 2026 than in the prior year, subject to member approval at the 91st AGM. Earnings are retained in the business rather than earmarked to reserves - the Directors do not propose to transfer any amount to the General Reserves for the year under review. The Company states it has no convertible instruments outstanding. Governance of capital and risk rests with the Board, supported by an Audit Committee empowered to scrutinise inter-corporate loans and investments, approve related party transactions, review the end use of funds raised through public offers and evaluate internal financial controls and risk management systems, and a Risk Management Committee overseeing the risk management policy and business continuity planning.|Committed to contributing to India's goal of Net-Zero emissions by 2070, with climate action, energy and emission management identified as a material opportunity in the BRSR|Transitioned to cleaner fuels such as PNG and LPG for generators and furnaces, and integrated electric forklifts for material handling|Installed on-grid solar capacity across key units - a 1 MWp plant at Matia, 650 KWp at Maddur, 600 KWp at Lucknow and a 62 KWp solar plant at the Kolkata Head Office|Transitioned to energy-efficient lighting solutions such as LEDs and natural ventilation to lower dependence on grid electricity and consequently reduce Scope 2 emissions|Waste management strategy built on reduce, recycle, recover and reuse, with all waste streams categorised and managed under defined SOPs for complete traceability and disposal compliance|Plastic waste, e-waste and hazardous waste managed for recyclability through certified recyclers, with all plants complying with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) guidelines|Optimising product size and packaging to reduce material consumption without compromising performance or durability|Strengthened EPR processes by filing the Annual Return for the defined target in FY 2025-26 under Battery Waste EPR requirements|Expanding high-efficiency and rechargeable product ranges as a practical means of reducing environmental impact|Closed operations at the Noida manufacturing unit during FY 2025-26, with voluntary separation of permanent workers at that unit|Structured grievance redressal and a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower framework covering employees, workers, communities, customers, shareholders and value chain partners, with community development executives positioned across plant locations|Strengthening governance and compliance architecture around BRSR, ESG and the DPDP framework as part of a forward-looking sustainability and data-protection approach
currentContext.expansion: The defining expansion of FY 2025-26 was the commissioning of Eveready's greenfield alkaline battery manufacturing facility at Jammu, undertaken under the 'Make in India' programme and the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' vision. It is a strategic investment of around Rs 200 crore, described by the Company as India's only operating alkaline battery facility, with an annual installed production capacity of 456 million units and a peak annual production capacity of approximately 360 million units. Management expects the plant to reduce import dependence, enhance supply chain resilience and improve margin efficiencies, and to open up white labelling business and supply to domestic and various international markets - reinforcing the stated ambition to emerge as a global player in alkaline batteries. Eveready's manufacturing footprint otherwise remains spread across units at Matia, Lucknow, Haridwar, Maddur and Kolkata, with an R&D facility at Kolkata; during the year the Company sold a parcel of factory land at Noida. In flashlights, the Company says it has proactively augmented production capacity to create headroom for incremental demand ahead of BIS-driven formalization of the category, and continues a focused rollout of a differentiated rechargeable portfolio. Category expansion continues through the mosquito swatter segment, where Eveready is category leader, and through calibrated, small-scale launches of chargers and power banks that lay the foundation for future expansion in adjacent categories. No further named capex projects, budgets or commissioning timelines are disclosed in the routed sections.

risks.risk: Structural pressure from a large unorganised segment in flashlights
risks.note: The category faces market fragmentation and persistent price competition, with consumers often prioritising price over product quality and features; the Company relies on brand equity, product differentiation and disciplined channel management to defend value.

risks.risk: Low-cost, sub-standard imports and erosion of quality benchmarks in flashlights
risks.note: Exposure to cheap non-compliant imports underscores dependence on regulatory enforcement (BIS Quality Control Order) to sustain the competitive advantage of quality-compliant branded players.

risks.risk: Low barriers to entry and unorganised competition in lighting and electricals
risks.note: The market continues to attract new players with competitive pricing strategies, causing persistent pricing pressure and fragmentation, only partially offset by Eveready's brand strength and distribution network.

risks.risk: Limited pricing power constraining margin sustainability
risks.note: In a highly competitive and price-sensitive environment the Company's ability to fully pass through input cost increases remains constrained; it maintains proactive vigilance on pricing to enable timely, calibrated pricing actions while balancing competitiveness with margin protection.

risks.risk: Failure to anticipate or respond quickly to changing consumer preferences
risks.note: In lighting and electricals, sustained success depends on continuous innovation and high product quality; a slow response could lead to loss of market relevance, mitigated through a product development framework and a broader SKU portfolio, especially in luminaires.

risks.risk: Market volatility, regulatory change, cybersecurity and operational disruption
risks.note: Identified by the Board as key risks tracked continuously through monitoring mechanisms and internal controls, with regular reviews by the Board and the Risk Management Committee.

risks.risk: Evolving regulatory and disclosure obligations (BRSR, ESG, DPDP framework)
risks.note: The Company is strengthening its governance and compliance architecture with increased focus on these and other emerging mandates, reflecting rising compliance burden across sustainability and data protection.

risks.risk: Non-compliance with waste management and Battery Waste EPR requirements
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as exposing the Company to significant financial penalties, loss of registration, operational disruptions and reputational damage; mitigated by strengthened EPR processes including filing the Annual Return for the defined target in FY 2025-26.

one-line thesis: Eveready commissioned India's only domestic alkaline battery plant in Jammu (INR 200cr capex) to shift from imports to local production, aiming to capture the 20%+ CAGR alkaline segment while using INR 251cr Noida land sale proceeds to aggressively reduce debt. Despite steep zinc cost inflation pressuring margins, the company guided for stable ~11.5% EBITDA margins in FY27 via pricing actions and mix shift to premium alkaline/lithium products.
financial scorecard: Revenue +8.2% YoY; EBITDA +8.9% YoY with 11.5% margin; PAT impacted by INR 500cr ICD provision write-off (creating business loss to offset capital gains); Order Book: N/A (FMCG/Discretionary); Net Debt reduced by >INR 100cr in FY26, targeting further reduction via INR 251cr Noida plot sales (INR 116cr realized, INR 136cr pending).
guidance: Revenue: High single-digit growth driven by alkaline volume doubling; Margin: Defend ~11.5% EBITDA despite zinc/crude headwinds; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: Jammu plant (INR 200cr) commissioned, no major new capex planned beyond routine.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Demand driven model; Focus on inventory optimization and working capital discipline.
segment / subsidiary detail: Batteries (66% of mix): +9.3% growth, Alkaline now 10% of battery mix (growing 20%+ CAGR), Carbon Zinc flat/low single digit; Flashlights (+3%): Rechargeable focus, BIS mandate tailwind; Lighting (+8.1%): Double-digit Q4 growth, sustainable momentum; Adjacencies: Mosquito racquets (leader in urban), Power banks/Chargers launching.
growth verticals / optionality: Alkaline saliency expected to rise from 15% to 20-25% in 3 years; Jammu plant enables white-labeling for global markets; Premiumization via Lithium batteries (INR 500/pair) and high-end flashlights (>INR 500); BIS norms to consolidate unorganized flashlight market share.
margins & cost dynamics: Zinc prices surged 20%+ creating significant headwinds; Mitigated via calibrated price hikes in Carbon Zinc/Alkaline, forex hedging (INR 83-95 volatility), and Jammu plant cost efficiencies; A&P spend steady at ~10% of sales.
capex / expansion: INR 200cr invested in Jammu facility (360mn alkaline capacity peak); Commercial production started May 2026; Expected operational breakeven in Year 1 at 100mn+ units; Payback period 5-6 years.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Debt reduction (targeting significant drop via INR 251cr asset sale proceeds); Priority 2: Funding organic growth internally; Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but balance sheet strengthening emphasized.
risks & watch-items: Sustained zinc/crude inflation above $100/barrel; Rupee depreciation to INR 95 impacting import costs; Geopolitical tension in West Asia disrupting supply chains; Potential cannibalization of Carbon Zinc volumes by Alkaline (managed via premiumization).
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Disciplined on cost/pricing; Strategic focus on manufacturing self-reliance and deleveraging; Transparent on tax transitions (moving to 22% regime in FY27 post-loss utilization).
non-obvious takeaways: INR 500cr ICD provision write-off created a business loss allowing tax-free offset of INR 104cr capital gain from Noida land sale; Jammu plant is the ONLY operating alkaline facility in India, creating a unique moat for import substitution and potential global white-labeling; Management expects alkaline to reach 1/3 of total battery category in 5-10 years.

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.
